# Privacy Policy for Jet Lag

**Effective date: 2 September 2026** — applies to version 1.9.0 onwards.

Jet Lag is a jet-lag planning app. This policy explains exactly what the app
does and does not do with your information. It is written to describe the
app's actual behaviour, not to reserve rights we don't use.

Two things described below are live for the first time in 1.9.0: the optional
flight lookup, and the one-time paid unlock. Earlier builds shipped with both
switched off, so the app made no network requests at all — these sections now
describe something you can actually reach.

The flight lookup section has also been corrected. It previously named only
AeroDataBox as the recipient; the request in fact goes to API.Market first,
which forwards it. Both are now named, because the company that receives your
data is exactly the thing a privacy policy exists to tell you.

**The short version:** Jet Lag has no accounts and no servers. Everything you
enter stays on your device. The only information that ever leaves your device
is a flight number and date, and only at the moment you tap "Look up".

---

## Information stored on your device

The app stores the following locally, on your device only:

- **Your sleep preferences** — your usual bedtime and wake time, your home
  time zone, and whether you want melatonin and caffeine guidance included in
  your plans.
- **Your trips** — trip names, and for each flight the origin and destination
  airports and the departure and arrival times you entered.
- **App state** — whether you've completed the intro, whether your free trip
  has been used, and whether you've purchased the paid unlock.

This information is held in the app's private storage. **It is not uploaded,
backed up to us, shared, or sold.** We never receive it, because there is no
"us" on the receiving end: the app has no server and no account system.

We are aware that sleep times and melatonin or caffeine preferences are
sensitive. That is precisely why they never leave your device.

To delete all of it, uninstall the app, or use your device's "clear app data"
option on Android.

## Information sent off your device

### Flight lookup (optional)

If you type a flight number and tap **Look up**, the app sends **that flight
number and the departure date** off your device in order to fetch the airports
and scheduled times.

**Two companies are involved, and you should know both.** The request goes to
**API.Market**, an API marketplace, at `prod.api.market`. API.Market passes it
on to **AeroDataBox**, the flight schedule service that actually answers it. We
hold an account with API.Market rather than with AeroDataBox directly, so
API.Market is the company your request reaches first.

- This happens **only** when you actively tap "Look up". It never happens in
  the background.
- Nothing else is sent — no identifier, no account, no other trip data, and
  nothing about your sleep preferences.
- As with any internet request, API.Market receives your device's IP address,
  and may pass it on.
- The feature is entirely optional. You can enter every flight by hand and the
  app never contacts the network at all.

**API.Market's and AeroDataBox's own privacy terms** govern what each of them
does with the requests they receive. We have no control over either.

### Purchases

The paid unlock is processed by **Apple's App Store** or **Google Play**, not
by us. Payment happens inside the store's own flow. We never see or receive
your payment details, card information, billing address, or store account
identity. The app only ever learns whether a purchase exists.

Apple's and Google's privacy policies govern those transactions.

## What the app does not do

- **No accounts.** There is nothing to sign up for and no password.
- **No analytics or tracking.** The app contains no analytics, telemetry,
  advertising, attribution, or crash-reporting SDKs of any kind.
- **No advertising**, and no sharing of data with advertisers.
- **No sale of personal information.**
- **No location access.** The app never requests or reads your device location.
- **No contacts, photos, calendar, microphone, or camera access.**
- **No push notifications from a server.** Reminders are scheduled locally on
  your device by the app itself and are not sent from anywhere.

## Permissions

Android apps declare permissions both for their own features and by inheriting
them from the libraries they use. Below is the complete picture, because a
partial list isn't an honest one.

### What the app uses directly

- **Internet / network state** — for the optional flight lookup described
  above. With no lookup, the app makes no network requests at all.
- **Notifications** — to show your plan's reminders at the right times, and to
  update the app's icon badge.
- **Vibration and wake** — so a reminder can alert you when your device is idle.
- **Run after device restart** — so reminders you've already scheduled survive
  a reboot and still fire. Used only to re-register those reminders.
- **Billing** — to offer the one-time paid unlock through Google Play. Payment
  is handled entirely by Play; see "Purchases" above.

### Inherited from libraries, and unused

The notification library we use bundles Google's Firebase Cloud Messaging and a
launcher-badge helper. These add a number of permissions — badge permissions
for specific phone launchers (Samsung, Huawei, Sony, HTC, Oppo and others),
Firebase messaging permissions, and a Google Play install referrer permission.

**The app does not use the server-push capability these enable.** It never
registers for push notifications and holds no push token. Firebase is not
configured in this app — the configuration file that would activate it is
deliberately absent, so Firebase does not start up and does not contact Google.
Every reminder you receive is scheduled locally on your device by the app
itself. The badge permissions are used only to update the number on the app's
own icon.

We list these because they are visible to anyone who inspects the app, and we
would rather explain them than have you wonder.

### What the app never requests

No location, contacts, photos, calendar, microphone, camera, or storage access.

## Children

Jet Lag is not directed at children and we do not knowingly collect
information from children.

## Medical disclaimer

Jet Lag provides general wellness guidance about sleep, light exposure,
melatonin, and caffeine timing. **It is not medical advice and is not a
medical device.** Talk to a doctor if you have a sleep disorder, are pregnant,
or take any medication.

## Changes to this policy

If the app's data practices change, this policy will be updated and the
effective date above revised. Material changes will be noted in the app's
release notes.
